problem: Prior VLN agents encode each discrete panoramic view as a single ResNet feature, so many different instruction nouns (TV, table, couch) must be matched against the same view vector. Off-the-shelf VL-BERTs (e.g., UNITER) are built for one-round decisions such as VQA and lack the temporal context a multi-step POMDP like VLN needs.
motivation: Instructions refer to fine-grained object landmarks, relative directions (turn left/right) and room types (bedroom, kitchen). Matching words to object regions, and supervising direction and room semantics, should give better grounding. Room types are inferable from characteristic objects (sink means bathroom, microwave means kitchen), and directions are inferable from candidate heading and elevation.
key_idea: Encode words and per-candidate object regions (plus orientation) jointly with a UNITER-initialised BERT, and carry temporal context across steps with an LSTM over the fused [CLS] features. Add auxiliary losses for each candidate's relative direction, the next-step room type and the goal room type, so the agent knows where objects are and where it is going.
insight: The ablation (Table 4) shows the gains come mainly from recurrence and the direction loss. Making BERT sequential (row #1 to #2) raises REVERIE val-unseen SR from 9.50 to 15.1 and SPL from 7.7 to 13.3, and NDH val-unseen GP from 2.42 to 2.86, while slightly lowering NDH val-seen (4.00 to 3.80), i.e. it mostly improves generalisation and reduces overfitting. Adding the direction loss (#2 to #3) further lifts REVERIE unseen SPL from 13.3 to 16.9 and NDH unseen GP from 2.86 to 3.09. The room-type losses help NDH (3.09 to 3.30 unseen) but the next-room loss hurts REVERIE val-unseen (SPL 16.9 to 14.9; full model 15.1), because REVERIE instructions rarely mention intermediate rooms. So the reported full model is not the best REVERIE-unseen configuration.
method: Object-level initial embedding: word tokens get token, position and type embeddings. Object regions per candidate view (boxes taken from REVERIE) get Faster R-CNN (bottom-up) 2048-d features, a 7-d box position and a type embedding. The candidate orientation <sin θ, cos θ, sin φ, cos φ> becomes an extra token via an FC layer. Each navigable candidate forms its own [words; objects; orientation] sequence.

Transformer stem: U=12 transformer layers initialised from UNITER process all G_t candidate sequences in parallel with a mask. The [CLS] output H_{t,U}[0] is taken as each candidate's fused vision-language representation.

Sequential BERT (temporal context): E_t = Tanh(W_e·[CLS]) per candidate, then I_t = AvgPool over candidates. An LSTM(I_t, h_{t-1}, c_{t-1}) produces the temporal state carried to the next step. This avoids feeding all previously seen objects back into BERT.

Room-and-direction multi-task heads: MLPs on E_t predict the action logit and the 4-way relative direction (left/right/front/back) of each candidate. MLPs on I_t predict the next-step room type, the goal room type (GT labels from Matterport3D region annotations) and a progress monitor as in AuxRN.

Training: EnvDrop-style mixed IL+RL (A2C). L = L^RL + λ3·L^IL, with L^IL = L^D + λ1·L^Rn + λ2·L^Rg + L^a + L^p, and λ1 = λ2 = λ3 = 0.2. AdamW with lr 1e-6 on 8 V100s; a separate model is trained per task.
REVERIE grounding: after navigation stops, the target object is selected with MAttNet, as in the REVERIE baseline.

setting.backbone: 12-layer transformer initialised from UNITER + LSTM + MLP heads (fine-tuned end-to-end); object features from a frozen bottom-up Faster R-CNN; MAttNet for REVERIE object grounding
setting.training_data: Per-task training sets. R2R: R2R train + EnvDrop augmented data. REVERIE and NDH/CVDN: original training data only. Transformer initialised from UNITER, which is pre-trained on COCO, Visual Genome, Conceptual Captions and SBU. No VLN-specific pre-training (unlike PREVALENT).
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 discrete views), represented as object regions (Faster R-CNN features + box geometry) within each candidate view, plus candidate heading/elevation
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select a navigable candidate or the current location to stop)
setting.privileged: Object bounding boxes are taken from REVERIE's annotations (derived from Matterport3D object annotations) and used as object regions at test time on all three tasks. Room-type GT from Matterport3D is used only for training supervision.

results: On REVERIE, ORIST roughly doubles the previous best on val-unseen: SPL 15.14 vs 7.19 and RGSPL 7.58 vs 4.67 for Nav-Pointer. On REVERIE test it reaches SPL 18.97 / RGSPL 9.28 vs 11.61 / 6.08. It is second on val-seen (SPL 42.21 vs Nav-Pointer 45.50). On NDH it is best in all settings, e.g. test-unseen Navigator GP 3.17 vs CMN 2.26 and PREVALENT 2.39. On R2R it gets test SPL 52 (SR 57), edging AuxRN and PREVALENT (51), although on val-unseen it trails PREVALENT (SR 57 vs 58, SPL 51 vs 53).
limitations: Relies on REVIERE-provided annotated object bounding boxes, which come from Matterport3D annotations, rather than a detector's proposals. This is effectively privileged object localisation, even on R2R and NDH.

Task-specific heads can hurt: the next-room-type loss degrades REVERIE val-unseen (SPL 16.9 to 15.1), and the reported full model is not the best unseen configuration. REVERIE val-seen navigation is below Nav-Pointer.
Separate models per task with no VLN-specific pre-training. NDH uses only the oracle's answer, not the full dialogue. REVERIE object grounding is delegated to an off-the-shelf MAttNet.
